Call path: `products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:161-176` — `user_settings` serializes `ReviewUserSettingsSerializer` on both GET and PATCH, and `get_stamphog_connected` (settings.py:72-81) calls `has_reviewable_repo_config(instance.team_id)` with no cache in between. `products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125` is a single `StamphogRepoConfig.objects.for_team(team_id).filter(enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False).exclude(installation_id="").exists()`; `team_id` is `BigIntegerField(db_index=True)` (products/stamphog/backend/migrations/0001_initial.py:21) so it is an indexed point lookup that short-circuits on the first row. Outage shape: the stamphog DB uses the fail-open engine with a Redis circuit breaker (posthog/settings/data_stores.py:176-190: threshold 3, cooldown 30s, probe timeout 5s; posthog/db_circuit_breaker.py:36-48 fails fast while open with a single half-open probe), so a stamphog outage costs one fast breaker check plus a `logger.exception` line per request — bounded, and exactly what the fail-soft comment at settings.py:73-76 chose.
votes.refutation: The claim reduces to "one indexed exists() on a second database per user-initiated settings read should be cached." Nothing bounds it because nothing needs to: the query is O(1) with an index, runs once per Code review tab open next to five heavier list calls on the same mount, and during an outage the breaker already makes it fail fast. Adding a 30-60s cache would introduce a real UX regression the finding hand-waves away: `stamphog_connected` exists precisely to flip the toggle from disabled to enabled the moment a user connects the Stamphog GitHub App (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066), and a stale False after connecting is worse than the microseconds saved. The remaining point (traceback per request while the breaker is open) is log noise during an outage window, not a correctness, availability, or scale problem. This is an optimization preference with no reachable trigger at real-world frequency, not a defect.
